h: מוֹצָאֵי יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, ה׳ Motzei Yom Kippur, 5

p: make known to us the path of life;
from poverty and lowliness extract us."
הֲגַם שֶׁאֵין מִדָּה יָפָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כַּעֲנִיּוּת
Although there is no trait as becoming to Israel as poverty,
and as it says in the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 71:1):
the verse is speaking of Israel" —
that he has nothing of his own,
only what Hashem Yisbarach has graciously given him —
that is a very fine trait;
but one who is poor in essence,
וּכְעִנְיַן אֲמָרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (נְדָרִים מא, א)
"There is no poor man except in knowledge" —
"Make known to me the path of life."
for through yirah lies the way
to arrive by means of it at the aspect of "life,"
which is words of Torah in essence,
"The fear of Hashem is the beginning of knowledge."
which are the two aspects that are the opposite
found in the knowledge of Torah.
וְשִׁפְלוּת הוּא הַהִיפּוּךְ שֶׁל יִרְאַת ה׳
And "lowliness" is the opposite of the fear of Hashem,
which is a path to life.
And this is "from day until night":
both at a time when it shines for him like day —
that I have nothing of my own —
for even if "I sit in darkness,
Hashem is a light for me" (Michah 7:8).
And to this one may also see an allusion
in the second song as well,
corresponds to the aspect of yirah,
which is called the "path of life,"
for he is the angel of the covenant,
to every aspect of the contrary desire,
"Because he was zealous for his God,"
and this is of the aspect of the fear of Hashem,
כִּי אָמַרְתִּי רַק אֵין יִרְאַת אֱלֹהִים
"For I said, surely there is no fear of God
and they will kill me on account of my wife."
is the aspect of the true life
that he asks for nothing but life,
"He asked life of You; You gave it to him —
length of days forever and ever."
And in the holiness of the Shabbos day
"And sanctified" is the aspect of the fear of Hashem,
from the desires of this world;
"and blessed" is the matter of the life
"The blessing of Hashem, it makes rich," etc.
that there flow to us from the holiness of Shabbos
for all the days of the week
that come upon us for good.
